question: How do I start a new Chulapa site on GitHub Pages?
expected: Recommend chulapa-101 as a personal blog template; create repository, enable Settings > Pages > GitHub Actions, set title/description/author/repository/url and commit to main or master. Workflow supplies base path; no local install or personal token required.

result.answer:
To start a new Chulapa site on GitHub Pages, use the Chulapa 101 starter template. Follow these steps:

1.  Visit [Chulapa 101 generator](https://github.com/dieghernan/chulapa-101/generate) to create your repository.
2.  Go to your GitHub repository **Settings > Pages**.
3.  Ensure the deployment source is set to **GitHub Actions**.
4.  Edit your `_config.yml` file to customize site details (title, description, author) in **Section A**.
5.  Commit your changes to the `main` or `master` branch.
6.  Wait for the GitHub Actions workflow to complete, then check your live site URL under **Settings > Pages**.

Note that Chulapa 101 is a personal blog template; you must replace the sample content, photos, and contact details with your own.

Source: [Installation guide](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/01-install)

question: How do I embed a local MP4 video? Give the Liquid include.

result.answer:
To embed a local MP4 video, use the `snippets/video.html` include with the `fileurl` parameter. Ensure the path is relative to your site root and uses the `relative_url` filter to correctly handle your `baseurl`.

```liquid
{% include snippets/video.html fileurl="/assets/mp4/sample.mp4" %}
```

**Next Steps:**
1. Upload your video file into your `assets/img/` or a dedicated video folder (e.g., `assets/mp4/`).
2. Replace `"/assets/mp4/sample.mp4"` in the code above with your actual filename and path.
3. Commit your changes to your publishing branch and wait for GitHub Actions to complete.

Source: [Adding videos](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/32-embed-video)

question: How do I enable a PhotoSwipe lightbox on a masonry gallery? Is there a page YAML option or Jekyll plugin, and does this work in v2.1.0?
expected: Development after v2.1.0 only. include_cached snippets/masonry.html internal="gallery" photoswipe=true; boolean Liquid include parameter, no page YAML setting or extra plugin. Default disabled, CDN assets load when an image is opened, original image links work without JavaScript. Each gallery isolated; keyboard/Escape/focus restoration and reduced motion. Also works for carousel.

result.answer:
To enable a PhotoSwipe lightbox on a masonry gallery, you must use the `photoswipe=true` parameter within the `include_cached` snippet. There is no page-level YAML option or Jekyll plugin for this feature.

Use the following Liquid code:

```liquid
{% include_cached snippets/masonry.html internal="gallery" photoswipe=true %}
```

**Important Version Note:** This feature is part of development after v2.1.0 and is **not available in the released v2.1.0**.

**Next Steps:**
1. Ensure you are using a development version (main) that supports PhotoSwipe.
2. Verify your internal image directory has the required `image_col: gallery` defaults.
3. Check that your gallery uses the `include_cached` snippet to ensure the lightbox assets load correctly.

Sources:
* [Layouts and snippets](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/04-layouts#masonry-gallery)
* [PhotoSwipe documentation](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/31-photoswipe)

question: Does the HTML theme version marker identify the exact commit and local overrides of my unpinned remote theme? Does v2.2.0 (unreleased) mean I can already install a published 2.2.0 release?
expected: No; inspect remote_theme tag or resolved Gemfile.lock version; marker not exact unpinned commit or local overrides; verify latest publication separately. The unreleased suffix marks a development build: 2.2.0 is an unpublished candidate, v2.1.1-dev labels refer to its planned features, and the latest published release remains v2.1.0.

result.answer:
No, the HTML marker identifies neither an unpinned commit nor local overrides.

Regarding the version, you cannot install a published 2.2.0 release yet. The 2.2.0 candidate is currently unpublished; the latest published release is v2.1.0. The `v2.1.1-dev` labels refer to planned features in the `main` branch, not a released gem or tag.

**Next Steps:**
* To ensure stability, pin your remote theme to the latest published version in `_config.yml`: `remote_theme: dieghernan/chulapa@v2.1.0`.
* To check your current theme version, refer to your `Gemfile.lock`.

Sources:
* [Release preparation](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs)
* [Remote-theme installation](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/20-remote-theme)
* [Custom hooks and version checks](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/44-custom-head)

question: I finished the first browser-only Chulapa tutorial. Which guided exercise publishes My photo walk, which file and image does it use, and how do I add its menu link without replacing the existing menu?
expected: Route to https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/59-photo-page-tutorial. Prerequisite: published Chulapa 101 blog and existing assets/img/madrid-at-night.jpg. Create _pages/photo-walk.md with layout default, header_type base, title My photo walk and permalink /photo-walk/; image uses relative_url and meaningful alt text. Add Photo walk with url /photo-walk/ to existing navbar.nav after Categories, retaining other entries and without a repository prefix or second navbar section. Commit to publishing branch, wait for Actions and check the public menu/page/image. Do not claim actual participant success.

result.answer:
The second browser tutorial guides you through publishing the **"My photo walk"** page.

*   **File to create:** `_pages/photo-walk.md`
*   **Image used:** `assets/img/madrid-at-night.jpg`

To add the menu link without replacing your existing menu, edit `_config.yml` and add the new entry to the existing `navbar.nav` list. You must match the indentation and retain all current entries.

**Example configuration:**
```yaml
navbar:
  nav:
    - title: Home
      url: /
    - title: Photo walk
      url: /photo-walk/
```

**Next Step:**
After committing both the new page and the updated `_config.yml` to your publishing branch, wait for GitHub Actions to succeed, then verify the new heading and image at the `/photo-walk/` URL via **Settings > Pages**.

Sources:
[Second browser tutorial](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/59-photo-page-tutorial)
[Basic editing and publishing](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/00-start)
[Navbar and footer configuration](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/02-config#navbar)
